title: The Reionization Photon Budget, Swept in Redshift

cards.heading: Does reionization have enough photons?
cards.body: Galaxies must leak enough ionizing radiation to reionize the universe. This study asks, across redshift, whether the leakage the literature assumes can actually close the budget. NebulaMind Lab.

cards.heading: The spread this work is about
cards.body: Published escape fractions against redshift. The scatter spans most of the physically allowed range.

cards.heading: The shape of the question
cards.body: For each redshift, compare the escape fraction the budget REQUIRES against the escape fraction observations INFER. A shortfall means the assumed leakage does not close reionization on its own.

cards.heading: z = 8.045
cards.body: the closure-crossing redshift, where the required and inferred escape fractions part company. Bootstrap bounds: 8.030 to 8.059.

cards.heading: 66 to 83 to 93
cards.body: percent of the probability mass in deficit as redshift climbs. The shortfall does not switch on; it deepens monotonically.
the crossing redshift in the least-favourable corner, where every assumption is set against the result. The shortfall strengthens rather than dissolving — it moves earlier, not later.

cards.heading: The trend is the result, not one redshift
cards.body: Three earlier drafts each reported a single redshift. They were superseded by one paper in which the trend across redshift is the spine, and the per-redshift numbers are table rows.

cards.heading: Refereed against its own arithmetic
cards.body: An independent reviewer re-ran the model rather than reading the changelog, reproduced the grid to sixteen decimal places, and returned MINOR with four precision-of-claim fixes — including that the title's threshold included a redshift where the paper's own criterion fails.

cards.heading: What this study does NOT establish
cards.body: It contains no measurements. The escape-fraction proxies are z~0.3 calibrations transported unchanged to the reionization era, and the shortfall fractions are conditional probabilities GIVEN those frozen anchors — not the probability that a real shortfall exists.

cards.heading: The escape route the authors name themselves
cards.body: If proxy transport fails — if low-redshift calibrations simply do not carry to these galaxies — the result goes with it. The paper names that as the only remaining way out, rather than leaving a reader to find it.

cards.heading: nebulamind.net
cards.body: A well-characterised number about a model of the literature. Stated as that, and not as a fact about the sky.
